newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end down, eroded by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end down, eroded by profit-taking.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended with moderate losses on Tuesday with prices eroded by profit-taking in the wake of a sharp rise the previous day, brokers said.
But they said interest remained strong in high-technology issues.
The Nikkei 225 ended at 20,069.41, down 159.31 points or 0.79 percent. Its September futures slipped 170 points to end at 20,070.
"A handful of high-techs issues, especially semiconductor-related issues, were active again today," said Noboru Yorita, Tachibana Securities general manager.

"There are also worries about how long the interest in semiconductor-related issues will last," a "Big Four" broker said. "Trade is gradually spreading to related issues but it remains to be seen if it will keep going,"

In late morning, Japan's Transport Ministry announced that it will list 1.5 million state-owned shares of Central Japan Railway Co (JR Tokai) on October 8. Of the total, 700,000 shares will be auctioned and the rest will be sold in the market through a secondary offering, it said.
There was no immediate effect on the market, but brokers worried that the listing could bog down the market.

"JR Tokai shares will pull funds out of the market, funds which were meant for other stocks," said a general manager at a medium-sized Japanese brokerage. "This is definitely bad news for the market and the index."

The TOPIX index shed 3.25 points or 0.21 percent to end at 1,521.89. The Nikkei 300 slipped 0.52 point or 0.18 percent to 295.91. The second section index fell 3.38 points or 0.19 percent to 1,815.30. The over-the-counter index was down 4.04 points or 0.34 percent at 1,181.34.
By sector, gas, services, air transport, electric power and transport equipment were the top gainers.
Fisheries, mining, oil, rubber and pulp/paper headed the list of decliners.
